solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 3 down to 4); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A vision of loveliness as I moved to end of quay

indicators.note: the clue tells us the letter I shifts along until it sits last in the word for a landing stage

parts.note: a quay is a landing place, like a pier

explanation.surface: Someone gazing at a beautiful figure as she walks to the far end of the harbourside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved to end of' takes the I in PIER and shifts it to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a beautiful fairy of Persian legend, hence any lovely sight.

clue.text: Charming chum treated roughly

parts.note: charming means pretty

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters of chum are processed and reworked

explanation.surface: A delightful friend who has been badly handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' looks like it belongs with 'treated', but it is the definition; 'treated' alone rearranges CHUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean approximately or nearly, an everyday idiom for an estimate.

clue.text: Specialised troops practise counterattack?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army's specialist engineering corps
to ply a trade is to practise it

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers rehearsing a counteroffensive.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: a retort counters a verbal attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort or response is a counter to someone's attack in argument.

clue.text: Architect initially welcomes housing staff's contracts

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of Architect is used
housing means the word for welcomes holds the word for staff within it

parts.note: welcomes means greets
staff, the workers, are men

explanation.surface: A building designer first greets the employees and hands them their contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: Contracts are formal deals, legally binding arrangements between parties.

clue.text: Golf organised, diversion avoiding key educational trip

parts.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
organised, as in managed, means ran

indicators.note: avoiding signals that the word for diversion does without one letter

parts.note: a diversion from the usual route is a detour
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A golf event was arranged, with a detour that skipped an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Tour was the cultural journey round Europe once taken by young wealthy Britons to complete their schooling.

clue.text: Up before court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Getting out of bed before a court appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright or standing is the sense shared by up and the answer.

clue.text: Sour red fruit, not quite ripe but golden inside

indicators.note: inside places the word for golden within the shortened word for ripe
not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ripe fruit is mellow
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A tart red fruit that is not fully ripe yet has golden flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: The morello is a dark, sharp-tasting variety of cherry used in cooking.

clue.text: Statesman's amended style of delivery

parts.note: something amended is new, revised
a yorker is a cricket delivery pitched at the batsman's feet

explanation.surface: A politician has changed the way they give speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' is not a politician but someone from a US state, here New York. A YORKER is a cricket ball bowled to land right at the batsman's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of New York State is a man of that state, a playful state's-man.

clue.text: Periodic losses suffered by skilled young swimmers

indicators.note: losing every other letter of skilled at regular intervals leaves alternate letters

explanation.surface: Talented junior swimmers suffer setbacks from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sild are young herrings, small fish canned like sardines.

clue.text: Revolutionary Indian instrument good for nothing

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the instrument's name is read backwards

parts.note: the sitar is a stringed Indian instrument

explanation.surface: A radical Indian musical instrument that is no good at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good for nothing' reads as one phrase, but 'good' is G and 'for nothing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of charge, costing nothing, is what the Latin-derived word means.

clue.text: Bowdlerise "pure" novel, wherein kiss has suggestion of scandal?

indicators.note: wherein places the kiss letter inside the shuffled word
novel means new, so the letters of pure take a fresh order, EPUR

parts.note: X is the conventional symbol for a kiss
-gate is the suffix tagged on to suggest a scandal, after Watergate

explanation.surface: Censoring a supposedly clean novel in which a kiss hints at impropriety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges PURE to EPUR; 'wherein' puts X into it, making EXPUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Bowdler cut offensive passages from Shakespeare, so to bowdlerise is to censor or purge a text.

clue.text: Swapping hands, put down part of spur

indicators.note: swapping means the two hand letters exchange places in the word for put down
hands are left and right, L and R, the two letters that trade places

parts.note: to put down is to lower

explanation.surface: Changing hands, someone lowers part of a horse rider's spur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swapping hands' exchanges the L and R in LOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowel is the spiked revolving wheel at the end of a rider's spur.

clue.text: Met secretly to destroy jockeys, with all love lost

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, so the remaining letters are shifted about
love is zero, the letter O, and every O in the phrase is removed

explanation.surface: A plot to wreck the riders, carried out without any affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with all love lost' strips both Os from TO DESTROY, leaving TDESTRY; 'jockeys' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a lovers' secret meeting, so to have trysted is to have met in private.

clue.text: Contributor to soap showing everyone in drag

indicators.note: in places the word for everyone inside the word for drag

parts.note: to drag something along is to tow it
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A soap opera cast member appears with everyone else in drag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soap' suggests a TV soap opera, but it is the washing kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow, rendered animal fat, is a traditional ingredient of soap and candles.

clue.text: Dessert's without charge, then?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the dessert word goes around the other

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert
a ward is someone in another's charge

explanation.surface: Is the pudding free of charge, then?
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside'. AFTERS is British slang for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Then, in the sense of later or next, is a synonym for subsequently.

clue.text: Condensed, as a walk in the park should be?

definitions.text: Condensed, as a walk in the park should be?

parts.words: Condensed, as a walk in the park should be?
parts.note: condensed suggests making something short, and a walk in the park is an easy task to dispatch quickly

explanation.surface: A shortened text, like an easy job ought to be.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase is 'abridged'; idiomatically, it means 'dealt with an easy task fast', which a walk in the park allows.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means dealt with something quickly and easily, which suits a trivially easy task.

clue.text: Wordsmith shot, craftsman runs away

parts.note: a shot of whisky is a dram

indicators.note: away signals that the runs letter is taken from the word for craftsman

parts.note: an artist is a skilled craftsman
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A writer is shot, and the artisan flees.
explanation.definitionFit: A playwright works with words, so is a kind of writer or wordsmith.

clue.text: Cook talented with cephalopods, primarily like squid

indicators.note: to cook the books is to fiddle them, so the letters are rearranged
primarily means only the first letter of cephalopods is used

explanation.surface: A skilled chef working with octopus and the like, mainly squid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges TALENTED plus the C from 'cephalopods primarily'.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid have tentacles, so they are described as having them.

clue.text: Reverend sat uneasily after fellow's precise testimony

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters following the word for fellow

parts.note: a chap is a fellow

indicators.note: uneasily suggests the letters of reverend sat are unsettled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman sits awkwardly after a man gives an exact account.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means exact citation of a source, as in naming the part and verse of a biblical passage.

clue.text: Piggy grabbing wine and hot snack

indicators.note: grabbing means the word for piggy holds the wine within it

parts.note: from the nursery rhyme 'this little piggy', where each piggy is a toe
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A greedy person helping themselves to wine and a warm bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piggy' looks like a glutton but is a toe, from the children's toe-counting rhyme 'This little piggy went to market'.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastie is a toasted sandwich, a British warm light meal.

clue.text: Seasonal meat cut with force at sea?

indicators.note: cut with means the meat word is split by the force abbreviation

parts.note: veal is calf meat
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A cut of meat suitable for the time of year, served forcefully at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The word relates to spring, so it is one particular season's adjective.

clue.text: Knight's advance across wide area

indicators.note: across means the advance word spans the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: to advance is to gain ground
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A knight moves forward over a large expanse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain is one of King Arthur's Round Table champions.

clue.text: Magnanimous knight served up joint, with wife away

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: away signals the wife letter leaves the word
in a down clue served up means the joint word is written bottom to top

parts.note: the elbow is a joint

explanation.surface: A generous knight serves a joint of meat after his wife has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns ELBOW to WOBLE; 'away' removes W.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous and high-minded in spirit are shared senses of both words.

clue.text: Current Lothario back on song

indicators.note: on means the reversed word follows the song word

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

indicators.note: back means the word for Lothario is read in reverse

parts.note: a womaniser, or wolf

explanation.surface: A seducer of the moment returns to singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'up to date', but it is a stream of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A current is a flowing movement, here of air.

clue.text: Doctor's check after fish has been brought up

indicators.note: after places the check abbreviation following
in a down clue brought up means the fish word reads upwards

parts.note: an eel is a fish
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A doctor's examination after someone has vomited fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' looks like vomited but signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leech is an old word for a physician, from the bloodsucking worms they used.

clue.text: Unknown insurgent worried Spartan character

parts.note: in algebra Z is an unknown quantity

indicators.note: insurgent means rebelling, so the letters revolt into a new order

parts.note: worried means ate, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: A mysterious rebel troubled a severe person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spartan' suggests austere, but means from Sparta, so a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeta is a letter of the Greek alphabet used in Sparta.

clue.text: Poet's material going west

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means the material word reads right to left

parts.note: toile is a linen fabric

explanation.surface: A writer's cloth is heading westwards.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was an American-born British poet.

clue.text: Minstrel with a pipe returned at end of dance

indicators.note: at end of puts the following letters after the word for dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: returned means the pipe word is written backwards

parts.note: a reed is a simple pipe

explanation.surface: A wandering singer with a flute returned when the dance finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer sings ballads, as minstrels did.

clue.text: Always keeping dry, he looked over, poised for action

indicators.note: keeping means the always word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: ay is an old word for always
TT, teetotal, means not drinking, dry
to look over a document is to read it

explanation.surface: Staying sober, he examined the plan, ready to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready to act immediately is the idiom's sense, like a weapon prepared.

clue.text: One particular man's on time

indicators.note: on means the man's word follows the time letter

parts.note: man's means belonging to him, his

explanation.surface: A specific person is punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstrative word picks out a specific one, singling it out.
